messages.subject: evasive movements and sample size
parts:
Hello all, a couple of questions, kind of new so I apoligize if these que=
stions are obvious. I'm studying a species of grouse and am concerned tha=
t some animals move prior to detection and do not flush at all. Histogram=
s of the distances recorded do not highlight evasive movements but perhap=
s this is because they are holding into the cover or moving beyond the fl=
ushing distance. Is there any way to account for this and might this bias=
my results to the point where the distance technique fails on this parti=
cular species??=20

Beyond the issues above, we also have a pretty low encounter rate; we flu=
sh about 20 birds per sample season. Am I wrong to want to pool data acro=
ss years to better model the detection process then use that global detec=
tion function to estimate abundance annually? Is this too simplistic or d=
oes there need to be statistical justification to pool across years to de=
velop a detection function? My thought is that because survey timing is t=
he same from year to year, w/ the same observers on the same transects, t=
he detection process should be consistent across years. Any thoughts woul=
d be greatly appreciated. DAVE
